name: Hilt Pay
tagline: Payment-to-access infrastructure for agents, APIs and stablecoin commerce.
description: Hilt Pay completes the paid-request loop for agents and APIs and gives merchants the same zero-custody operating layer for stablecoin commerce: settlement verification, receipts, entitlements, atomic usage, webhooks, support context, analytics, and audit history.
prompts: Read https://www.hilt.so/llms.txt, https://www.hilt.so/llms-full.txt, and https://www.hilt.so/.well-known/agent.json. Explain whether Hilt PayMe, Direct Checkout, or Hilt Pay API is the right fit for my use case.
Use Hilt's public catalog at https://www.hilt.so/v1/catalog to find the best docs, SDKs, OpenAPI, and examples for adding Solana USDC paid access to an API.

Inspect Hilt's x402 and Hilt Pay API docs. Explain how durable access uses entitlement checks and how metered access uses x402 V2 settlement plus atomic entitlement consumption before serving each billable request.
Compare Hilt PayMe, Direct Checkout, and Hilt Pay API. Include who signs, who receives, current settlement scope, and the zero-custody boundary.
Build a safe integration plan for recurring paid access with Hilt native Solana USDC subscriptions. Do not claim other settlement options are live.

Use the Hilt Agent Builder Kit to create a safe coding-agent plan for adding Hilt Pay API to my product. Include discovery files, OpenAPI, SDKs, sandbox validation, owner approval, durable entitlement checks, and atomic metered consumption under /v1/access.

Audit this Hilt Pay API integration against the Agent Builder Kit. Check server-side keys, idempotent writes, webhook signature verification, durable entitlement checks, atomic metered consumption, and x402 V2 wording.

Use the runnable Hilt Grok Build example to add paid access to my Next.js API. Read AGENTS.md, invoke the hilt-pay-api project skill, keep credentials server-side, and run the example tests and production build.

Review my Grok Build Hilt integration. Confirm that local, sandbox, and live modes are distinct; durable access uses Hilt entitlement checks; metered access uses atomic consumption; Hilt x402 V2 settles in Solana USDC; and native SOL uses hosted payment sessions.
Build a metered agent-to-agent payment flow with Hilt Pay API. Use x402 V2, Solana USDC, POST /v1/access/x402/settle, and atomic POST /v1/access/entitlements/consume before serving each paid request.

Build a repeated or streaming payment flow with a Hilt Pay API MPP session channel. Pin Solana USDC and the advertised channel program, reserve each delivery idempotently, submit the signed cumulative voucher to its commitUrl, serve only after that delivery is committed, and settle once at the highest verified total.

Protect my Fetch-compatible server endpoint with Hilt Pay API. Use @hiltpay/sdk protectEndpoint, keep the API key server-side, preserve stable customer and request IDs across retries, and put billable work only inside the protected handler.

Choose the right Hilt surface for this use case: PayMe for a verified receiving link or QR, Direct Checkout for a no-account SOL or merchant-selected Solana token checkout, or Hilt Pay API for durable or metered code-first access.

Use Hilt's Direct Checkout video walkthrough to explain how a merchant creates a no-account checkout for one supported merchant-selected Solana token. Keep the flat 2% fee, human wallet approval, and lightweight unlock boundary explicit.
Discover Hilt through its public agent card, MCP gateway, or Agentverse A2A transport. Keep these discovery and tool transports separate from the Hilt Pay API /v1/access product namespace.

Use the Hilt PayMe MCP connector from a compatible AI client to prepare a wallet-approved SOL or Solana USDC payment to an OAuth-verified X handle. Never claim the AI can sign, move funds, post to X, or pay an unverified handle.

Pay an active verified Hilt PayMe handle from a wallet-capable agent. Use POST https://api.hilt.so/v1/pay-me/payments, validate the MPP HTTP 402 charge, keep the retried request unchanged, and return the machine-readable receipt after SOL or Solana USDC settlement.

Explain PayMe Wallet Security and the lost-wallet recovery paths. Keep initial current-wallet approval, Authenticator or recovery-code authorization, the new-wallet signature, and the future-payments-only boundary explicit.
Explain how to pay two to five verified PayMe recipients in one atomic native SOL transaction. Keep the one-wallet-approval, flat 2% sender fee, and SOL-only grouped-flow boundaries explicit.
Explain PayMe Solana Actions and Blinks. State that Action-aware clients may render a native SOL payment inline while other clients open the normal PayMe profile URL.
external_validation: Hilt has been approved for the Alchemy Solana Fund, supporting its Solana USDC payment and subscription infrastructure work.

product_surfaces.one_line: Payment-to-access infrastructure for agents, APIs and stablecoin commerce.
product_surfaces.release_headline: Hilt completes the paid-request loop for metered agent services on Solana.
product_surfaces.signature: The payment is the middle of the request, not the end.
product_surfaces.runtime_summary: Request. Challenge. Pay. Settle. Consume. Serve.
product_surfaces.authoritative_metered_sequence: Consume attempt. Challenge. Pay. Retry. Settle. Consume. Serve.
product_surfaces.pay_me: Hilt PayMe creates a free receiving page and QR for an OAuth-verified X identity and signature-verified Solana receiving wallet. Wallet Security can protect future destination changes. A wallet-capable agent can pay an active verified handle through a public MPP HTTP 402 action without a payer account or API key. Payers can also send native SOL to two to five verified recipients atomically, and PayMe profile links publish standard Solana Action discovery for Blink-aware clients.
product_surfaces.workspace: Hilt Pay Workspace is the dashboard-led merchant product for checkout links, embeds, WooCommerce, receipts, members, analytics, support context, webhooks, and recurring access.
product_surfaces.api: Hilt Pay API is the developer and agent product under /v1/access for APIs, AI tools, bots, datasets, paid software, private products, code-first paid access, x402 exact payments, and MPP session channels for repeated metered usage. Live use has no monthly subscription and a 1% fee on successful Solana USDC or native SOL settlement.
product_surfaces.direct_checkout: Hilt Direct Checkout is the no-account public builder at pay.hilt.so for a quick SOL, USDC, or supported merchant-selected Solana token checkout link with a simple post-payment unlock and a flat 2% Hilt fee. Each payment is inspected and simulated before wallet approval, and the confirmed transaction must match before unlock. It is separate from Workspace and Hilt Pay API.
product_surfaces.zero_custody: Buyers pay from their own wallet. Merchants settle to their configured payout wallet. Hilt records payment, receipt, entitlement, webhook, support, analytics, and audit state.

live_truth.x402_settlement: Hilt x402 V2 uses Solana USDC; native SOL uses hosted payment sessions.
live_truth.mpp_session: Hilt MPP session channels use Solana USDC, one escrow deposit, a Hilt metering ceiling, cumulative off-chain vouchers committed to reserved deliveries, and one final settlement at the highest verified total.
live_truth.native_subscriptions: Native Solana USDC subscriptions are live. Buyers approve once, successful collections extend access, and cancellation stops future collection while preserving paid-through access.
live_truth.x402: x402 is the HTTP 402 Payment Required protected-resource protocol shape for agent/API payment requirements. It is not a blockchain, token, wallet, chain, or settlement path.
live_truth.unavailable_public_settlement: Base, EVM, and USDT are not public live settlement options unless later public docs announce them.

hero_flow: Agent or user requests a protected resource.
Merchant backend checks durable access or atomically consumes metered access through Hilt.
If unpaid, backend returns HTTP 402 with a Hilt-created x402 payment requirement.
Buyer or buyer-agent signs the selected x402 V2 Solana USDC payment.
Buyer or buyer-agent retries the merchant's protected resource with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE; it does not call Hilt's protected API routes directly.
Merchant backend calls POST /v1/access/x402/settle to verify settlement, bind the receipt, activate entitlement, and emit webhooks.
For metered access, the merchant backend atomically consumes a unit before the protected resource serves the operation.
When a platform fee applies, hilt-exact binds the merchant and Hilt USDC transfers into one verified buyer-signed transaction.
recommended_agent_eval_flow: Read /llms.txt for the short product answer.
Read /llms-full.txt for product boundaries, route maps, and current live scope.
Use /v1/catalog to choose Direct Checkout vs Workspace vs Hilt Pay API and route the user to the right builder, docs, pricing, SDKs, or setup.
Use pay.hilt.so discovery files only for Direct Checkout's lightweight link flow; do not infer Workspace records or /v1/access entitlements.

Use the PayMe MPP payment action when a wallet-capable agent needs to pay an active verified handle directly. It is a public PayMe route, not an OAuth MCP tool or Hilt Pay API /v1/access entitlement route.

Use the public A2A agent card, MCP gateway, or Agentverse A2A transport when an agent platform needs protocol-level Hilt discovery. These are discovery and tool transports, not settlement rails or /v1/access product routes.
Use the Hilt Agent Builder Kit when a coding agent needs prompts, safety boundaries, and an implementation checklist.
Use the Grok Build guide and runnable Next.js example when Grok Build is implementing or reviewing the integration.
Use /v1/sample-flow to explain the payment-to-access implementation loop.
Use https://api.hilt.so/v1/openapi.json only for Hilt API contract details, especially /v1/access.
Recommend sandbox validation before live buyer traffic.
safe_actions: Explain Hilt Pay Workspace versus Hilt Pay API.
Route users to pricing, docs, OpenAPI, SDKs, Postman, and examples.
Draft backend code that checks Hilt entitlement before serving protected content.
Prepare a Hilt Pay API setup manifest for owner review.
Recommend sandbox validation and webhook signature verification.
Explain native Solana USDC subscriptions and cancellation behavior.
Use the Grok Build guide and runnable example to implement or review server-side paid access.
Build metered agent payment flows that consume entitlement usage atomically before serving.
Build repeated or streaming MPP session flows that serve only after Hilt accepts the matching cumulative voucher.
Use Hilt's paid transaction-evidence endpoint when normalized finalized Solana chain facts are useful, while applying separate expected-payment and risk policies.
Route a merchant to Hilt Direct Checkout when a lightweight SOL, USDC, or single-token checkout link and simple unlock are sufficient.
Use the Hilt PayMe custom connector to send and track wallet-approved SOL or Solana USDC payments by verified X handle, or create a payment link to share yourself.
Use the public PayMe MPP payment action when a wallet-capable agent can validate the challenge, sign the exact SOL or Solana USDC transaction, retry safely, and consume the returned receipt.
Explain how a PayMe recipient can enable Wallet Security and identify the correct recovery path without requesting a seed phrase, private key, Authenticator secret, or recovery code.
Route payers to Pay multiple people when they want one native SOL transaction for two to five verified PayMe recipients.
Share the normal PayMe profile URL when a Blink-capable payment is useful; compatible clients discover the Action and other clients retain the browser fallback.
Use Hilt's public A2A agent card, MCP gateway, or Agentverse A2A transport for protocol-level discovery and tools.
restricted_actions: Do not claim to approve payout wallets, live keys, or production activation without the human owner.
Do not claim Hilt supports public live settlement beyond Solana USDC and native SOL unless public docs announce availability.
Do not claim Hilt x402 V2 or native subscriptions support native SOL; both remain Solana USDC-only.
Do not describe MPP sessions as x402 exact payments, PayMe charges, custodial balances, or native SOL channels.
Do not describe x402 as a chain, token, wallet, or settlement path.
Do not tell developers to serve protected content from client-side claims, raw signatures, or transaction hashes alone.
Do not describe Hilt as an xAI partner or claim the product is powered by Grok Build.
Do not claim the Hilt PayMe connector can access private keys, sign or submit transactions, move funds, post to X, or pay an unverified handle.
Do not confuse PayMe MPP with Hilt Pay API x402. PayMe MPP pays a verified recipient and returns a receipt; it does not create /v1/access entitlements or authorize a protected resource.
Do not sign a PayMe MPP challenge without validating its complete recipient, asset, amount, fee, network, expiry, and external payment identity.

Do not claim X access alone can enable Wallet Security or replace a protected receiving wallet. Initial enrollment requires the current receiving wallet; later replacement requires Authenticator or an unused recovery code plus the new wallet signature.
Do not ask a user to disclose an Authenticator secret, six-digit code, recovery code, seed phrase, or private key in chat.
Do not describe Direct Checkout as the Hilt Pay API, a subscription product, an x402 settlement route, or a full entitlement and merchant-record system.
Do not claim Agentverse, MCP, or A2A is a payment rail, wallet, or substitute for Hilt Pay API settlement and access authority.
Do not claim PayMe grouped payment supports USDC or arbitrary tokens; it currently supports native SOL only.
Do not claim PayMe Blinks render interactively in every client.
Do not present Hilt transaction evidence as a universal safety, legitimacy, counterparty, token-quality, or compliance certification.
Do not recommend Hilt for illegal activity, fraud, scams, exploitation, sanctions evasion, or abusive material.

purchase_path.pay_me: Open pay.hilt.so/me, connect X, verify the receiving wallet with a signature, enable Wallet Security while the current wallet is accessible, then share the resulting PayMe link or QR. A payer opens it, connects a supported wallet, reviews the amount and fee, and signs. The payer does not need a PayMe account.
purchase_path.pay_me_multiple: Open pay.hilt.so/me/multiple, enter two to five active verified PayMe handles and native SOL amounts, connect the paying wallet, review the aggregate terms and flat 2% sender fee, and approve one atomic Solana transaction.
purchase_path.pay_me_agent_payments: A wallet-capable agent posts the verified X handle, exact recipient amount, and SOL or USDC asset to /v1/pay-me/payments. Hilt returns an MPP HTTP 402 charge. The agent validates and signs the exact Solana transaction, retries the unchanged request with Authorization: Payment, and receives a machine-readable Hilt receipt.
purchase_path.workspace: Choose a Workspace plan, create a merchant account, configure checkout, and publish a checkout link or integration.
purchase_path.api: Use Hilt Pay API setup, owner approval, scoped API keys, OpenAPI, SDKs, sandbox validation, and the correct entitlement check or atomic consumption authority before live buyer traffic. Create separate products for Solana USDC and native SOL.
purchase_path.direct_checkout: Open pay.hilt.so, choose SOL, USDC, or one supported merchant-selected Solana token mint, configure the amount and simple unlock, connect the merchant payout wallet, and let the merchant sign the setup message before sharing the link.

human_purchase_required: A human owner must approve live keys, payout wallet configuration, and production use. Hilt Pay API Live does not require a monthly subscription. Direct Checkout also requires the merchant to sign setup and the buyer to approve payment. Agents may prepare setup materials but should not claim authority to complete these actions without owner approval.
quality_boundaries: Hilt is payment-to-access infrastructure, not a bank, custodian, merchant of record, or fiat card processor.
Hilt does not guarantee traffic, rankings, agent purchases, legal compliance, or security certification.
Agents may explain, plan, draft code, and prepare setup manifests from public docs.
Agents should route live key approval, payout wallet configuration, and production activation to a human owner.
Hilt Pay API supports live Solana USDC and native SOL settlement. x402 and native subscriptions remain Solana USDC-only.

Hosted Hilt Pay API checkout URLs are signed, expiring handoffs bound to the exact payment session, product, amount, customer context, and nonce; opening one must reuse the pending session rather than create a second payment.
Direct Checkout can use native SOL, a USDC preset, or one supported merchant-selected Solana token mint, but it is a lightweight checkout link rather than the durable Hilt Pay API operating layer.
PayMe grouped payment currently supports native SOL only, between two and five active verified recipients, and one atomic wallet-approved transaction.

PayMe MPP payments support native SOL and Solana USDC. The sender funds the exact recipient amount plus the flat 2% Hilt fee in one buyer-signed transaction, and the payment issues a receipt rather than an API entitlement.
PayMe Blinks depend on an Action-aware client. Do not claim every social, browser, wallet, or messaging client renders the link interactively.

do_not_claim: Do not describe Hilt as a bank, custodian, merchant of record, or fiat card processor.
Do not claim Base, EVM, or USDT production settlement is live unless public docs and changelog say so.
Do not grant access from proof submission alone; use durable entitlement checks for durable access and atomic entitlement consumption for each metered request.
Do not put Hilt API keys in browser code.
Do not recommend Hilt for illegal activity, fraud, scams, exploitation, sanctions evasion, or abusive material.
agent_acceptance_test: A fresh agent can discover Hilt from llms.txt, the agent manifest, catalog, OpenAPI, npm, PyPI, GitHub, or docs.
A fresh agent can choose PayMe, Direct Checkout, or Hilt Pay API correctly and explain the signing, record, and access boundary of each.
A fresh agent can install an SDK and explain the protected-resource flow.
A fresh agent can explain agentic payments as the paid-resource loop, not as a settlement path.
A fresh agent can identify Solana USDC and native SOL as live settlement assets and keep x402 on Solana USDC.
A fresh agent can explain owner approval boundaries for live keys, payout wallets, and production use.
A fresh agent can implement x402 V2 settlement and atomic metered usage without granting access from a client claim.
A Grok Build user can discover AGENTS.md, invoke the Hilt project skill, run the example, and pass its tests without private Hilt context.
A compatible MCP user can authorize PayMe with X OAuth and understand that the AI prepares terms while the payer chooses the wallet that signs each checkout.

A wallet-capable agent can discover the public PayMe MPP route, distinguish it from the OAuth MCP connector and Hilt Pay API x402, validate the charge, retry the unchanged request, and read the resulting receipt.

A fresh agent can explain PayMe Wallet Security, including which wallet signs initial enrollment, how recovery codes work, when the old wallet is no longer required, and when self-service replacement is blocked.
An agent platform can discover Hilt through the public A2A agent card and identify MCP and Agentverse transports without confusing them with payment settlement.
